subject: Architecture
title: Notre-Dame de Paris: Fire and Rebirth
description: A micro-lesson that makes Notre-Dame de Paris: Fire and Rebirth usable.

hook.text: On April 15, 2019, Notre-Dame's spire collapsed in flames as the world watched live.

buildup.text: The cathedral was begun in 1163. Its twin towers, rose windows, and flying buttresses define Gothic design.

discovery.text: The 'forest' — 1,300 oak beams in the roof — dated from the 12th century. Each beam was a single tree.

twist.text: The fire melted 300 tons of lead from the roof. Cleanup required hazmat suits and years of decontamination.

climax.text: A €846 million restoration rebuilt the spire and roof. Notre-Dame reopened in December 2024.

punchline.text: 860 years of faith, one night of fire, and a nation rebuilt it in five.

quiz.question: What was the 'forest' inside Notre-Dame?
options: A garden courtyard inside the cathedral walls
1,300 oak beams in the roof, each from a single tree
A collection of carved wooden statues in the nave

details.summary: The April 2019 fire at Notre-Dame destroyed the medieval oak roof and 19th-century spire, but the stone vaults largely held, protecting most of the interior and stained glass.
details.whyItMatters: Notre-Dame's fire and restoration revealed how deeply sacred buildings are embedded in collective identity. The global grief and billions in donations showed that a cathedral can be sacred to an entire civilization, not just its congregation.
takeaways: 2019 fire destroyed the medieval roof and 19th-century spire
Stone vaults held, protecting most of the interior contents
Over 1,000 craftspeople completed restoration in five years

faq.question: What traditional techniques were used in the Notre-Dame reconstruction?
faq.answer: The roof was rebuilt using hand-hewn oak timbers shaped with traditional adze and axe techniques. Lead covering was cast and applied by hand. Stone carvers replaced damaged elements using hand tools. Modern laser scanning guided placement while traditional craft ensured authenticity.

faq.question: How much did the restoration cost?
faq.answer: Approximately 700 million euros were donated from around the world within days of the fire. Major French luxury companies, the French government, and hundreds of thousands of individuals contributed. The rapid fundraising demonstrated the cathedral's unique position as a global cultural monument.
